title: Week 16 Mastery Quiz · Iran, Brazil, and South Africa

questions.question: A fictional Brazilian coalition holds 260 of 513 legislative seats. Under a simple-majority rule, what follows?
options: It exceeds the 257-seat simple-majority threshold, but other voting rules may apply to particular measures.
260 seats falls below a 256-seat threshold.
A simple majority automatically satisfies constitutional amendment rules.
A coalition with 260 seats necessarily controls every judicial decision.
questions.explanation: It exceeds the 257-seat simple-majority threshold, but other voting rules may apply to particular measures.

questions.question: A researcher claims South Africa's constitutional equality guarantees that economic disparities have disappeared. What is the missing distinction?
options: A constitutional right automatically removes all unequal outcomes.
Legal rights and measured socioeconomic outcomes must be assessed separately.
Income inequality establishes that no equality protection exists.
Economic disparities can be measured directly from constitutional text.
questions.explanation: Legal rights and measured socioeconomic outcomes must be assessed separately.

questions.question: An analyst compares Iran's elected bodies with unelected oversight institutions. Which evidence best captures institutional authority?
options: Elected bodies necessarily have final authority over every decision.
Candidate screening is unrelated to representation.
Constitutional competencies, candidate screening, decision rules, and documented practice.
Constitutional titles alone establish each institution's effective power.
questions.explanation: Constitutional competencies, candidate screening, decision rules, and documented practice.

questions.question: A fictional Brazilian federal environmental policy is enforced unevenly across states. Which data would improve causal analysis?
options: Federal legislation guarantees identical local enforcement.
Local outcomes can be explained without administrative data.
Variation alone proves every state has different legal standards.
Subnational staffing, budgets, enforcement records, local conditions, and policy timelines.
questions.explanation: Subnational staffing, budgets, enforcement records, local conditions, and policy timelines.

questions.question: A South African source describes a post-apartheid reform without naming the adoption date. How should the student establish chronology?
options: Locate authenticated legal texts, historical records, effective dates, and subsequent amendments.
An undated summary is sufficient to establish legal effect.
A reform takes effect whenever its proposal is published.
All later amendments are irrelevant to the original reform.
questions.explanation: Locate authenticated legal texts, historical records, effective dates, and subsequent amendments.

questions.question: A political commentary groups Iran, Brazil, and South Africa together because all hold elections. What is the strongest methodological correction?
options: Holding elections guarantees unrestricted political competition.
Compare candidate access, constitutional constraints, political rights, competition, and accountability separately.
All three countries have identical unelected oversight institutions.
Different constitutions cannot meaningfully be compared.
questions.explanation: Compare candidate access, constitutional constraints, political rights, competition, and accountability separately.

questions.question: A simulated Brazilian poll samples only one metropolitan region to describe national attitudes. What caution applies?
options: Metropolitan attitudes automatically equal national preferences.
A large regional sample eliminates geographic coverage bias.
Single-region coverage cannot support unqualified national generalization.
National population size alone fixes sample bias.
questions.explanation: Single-region coverage cannot support unqualified national generalization.

questions.question: A research paper treats South Africa's truth-seeking processes as identical to criminal prosecution. Which distinction matters?
options: Truth-seeking commissions issue criminal convictions by definition.
Criminal prosecution and truth-seeking use identical legal standards.
Recording testimony always establishes individual criminal guilt.
Different bodies have different mandates, evidentiary practices, remedies, and legal powers.
questions.explanation: Different bodies have different mandates, evidentiary practices, remedies, and legal powers.

questions.question: A commentator asserts a single protest proves an entire country's preference. What evidence can improve the inference?
options: Participation scale, geographic reach, counterevidence, polling methods, and institutional response.
A visible protest represents a statistically random sample.
One demonstration proves every region favors the same position.
Crowd size alone proves a constitutional mandate.
questions.explanation: Participation scale, geographic reach, counterevidence, polling methods, and institutional response.

questions.question: A senior compares the three states using different years of rights indicators without disclosure. What revision preserves analytical integrity?
options: Different-year indicators are directly comparable without qualification.
Align years or identify the time mismatch and explain its influence on comparison.
A later indicator automatically supersedes an earlier one in all comparisons.
Year mismatches cannot affect institutional comparisons.
questions.explanation: Align years or identify the time mismatch and explain its influence on comparison.

shortResponse: How do constitutional design, identity, inequality, social movements, and political conflict shape different paths of change?
rubric: 10 points: precise claim (2), accurate concepts (2), two specific pieces of evidence (2), reasoning (2), counterargument or limitation (1), revision condition (1).
